standard.title: Leadership and decision-making
standard.description: devise, implement and refine strategies for decision-making when working in groups or teams that demonstrate leadership and collaboration skills
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can demonstrate fair play and reflect on how ethical behaviour influences outcomes (AC9HP10M08), and have previously practised and applied leadership, collaboration and group decision-making in physical activities (AC9HP8M09). At Y9-10 the focus shifts to devising, implementing and refining decision-making strategies — a higher-order planning and evaluation task.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students devise, implement and refine decision-making strategies for group and team contexts that demonstrate leadership and collaboration skills.

nodes.label: Devising decision-making strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can devise explicit strategies for group decision-making that demonstrate leadership and collaboration
nodes.minimum_width: Devise one strategy for making a group decision in a physical activity context; explain how it distributes leadership and incorporates different perspectives
nodes.typical_width: Devise decision-making strategies that incorporate leadership, collaboration and group dynamics; analyse leadership styles and group dynamics through initiative games; use self-talk and encouragement to motivate team members; evaluate their own contribution to teamwork and enjoyable participation
wider: Devise and implement a decision-making strategy for a complex group movement challenge — evaluate how the strategy performed under pressure and what adjustments were needed
Analyse different leadership styles (directive, collaborative, distributed) through initiative games — evaluate when each style is most effective and for which group composition
Design and implement self-assessment and peer-assessment tools to evaluate performance across multiple group roles — use findings to refine leadership approach
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot devise an explicit decision-making strategy cannot implement and refine one in Node 2 — refinement requires a concrete intended approach to evaluate against actual group outcomes.

response_modes.reason: Students commonly lead groups without making their decision-making strategy explicit — acting on instinct without articulating the approach. The investment is in making the strategy explicit: how will decisions be made in this group, what is each person's role, how will disagreement be handled. This articulation is prerequisite for implementation and refinement.

success_criteria: Articulates a specific decision-making approach — not just 'we'll discuss it'
Strategy includes a mechanism for incorporating different perspectives or resolving disagreement
Explains how leadership is distributed — who decides what, and how

nodes.label: Implementing and refining leadership strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can implement and refine decision-making strategies in group contexts, using assessment tools to evaluate and improve
nodes.minimum_width: Implement a devised decision-making strategy in a group activity; evaluate how well it worked and identify one specific refinement
nodes.typical_width: Implement and refine decision-making strategies across group and team contexts; use self-assessment and peer-assessment tools to evaluate performance in multiple roles; apply self-talk and encouragement to support persistence; evaluate their own contribution to teamwork quality and enjoyment for all
wider: Implement the same decision-making strategy across two different group contexts (e.g. different team sizes, different challenge types) and evaluate how the strategy needed to be adapted for each
Create a peer-assessment tool for evaluating leadership and collaboration; use it with a group member and use their feedback to refine your own leadership approach
Lead a group through an initiative problem and document the decision-making process in real time — evaluate the gap between the devised strategy and what actually happened, and propose refinements

response_modes.reason: Leadership and collaboration capability develops through implementing and refining strategies across multiple group contexts — different team sizes, different challenges, different group compositions. A single implementation does not produce transferable leadership capability. The assessment tools direction supports systematic reflection rather than impression-based evaluation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Cross-context implementation comparison, peer-assessment tool design, and real-time documentation each add dimensions of reflection and refinement that single-context implementation cannot produce. Students who engage the wider tier develop metacognitive awareness of their own leadership and decision-making — not just the ability to lead in one familiar context.
success_criteria: Implements the devised strategy — not just describes it
Evaluates a specific aspect of how the strategy performed — what worked and what didn't
Identifies a concrete refinement based on the evaluation, not a generic improvement
